classification_reasons: Spec tightness: now tight - the one flagged concern is closed by the owner ([x], decision recorded, merged via PR #6 whose merge commit 52df022 is authored by luissiviero), both intent open questions are answered, and Acceptance is measurable (percent(1, 4) == 25.0, percent(7, 100) == 7.0, pytest.raises(ZeroDivisionError), 5 passed, silent compileall, 'All checks passed!').

Blast radius is small: plan.md lists 3 files (sample_pkg/calc.py, sample_pkg/__init__.py, tests/test_calc.py), all additive; no schema, contract, configuration or migration change; none of sdlc.yaml's 4 risk_list items is touched (gate dry run at HEAD: 'no risk-list item touched').

Test coverage: percent does not exist yet, so no existing test covers the code the plan will add - the third routine criterion fails, hence non-routine (iteration cap 2; iterations is already 2 at HEAD, so a further fix round would hit the limit).
attempted: Intent: re-mapped spec.md Requirements/Design/Acceptance to intent.md Proposed outcome (signature, percent(1, 4) == 25.0, ZeroDivisionError on zero whole, __init__/__all__ export, normal + zero tests, three green targets) and Constraints (no dependency, add/divide untouched, test_flag untouched, no rounding, no guardrail edit). The new exactness requirement (percent(7, 100) == 7.0) is a precision of 'part as a percentage of whole', not a new feature, and it adds no rounding or formatting option. No scope drift found.

Spec and plan: `git show 23f9e5d` touches spec.md (Requirements, security-baseline sentence, Design, Open questions, Acceptance), plan.md (Files, step 1, step 3, Risks, Options not taken, Proof), run-b.json (start-run: new started_at) and status.yaml (iterations 1->2, updated_at) - parked_reason and gate.result are left for the gate, risk_accepted stays empty, no owner-only field was changed by automation. spec.md and plan.md now agree on `return divide(part * 100, whole)` and on the two test_percent assertions; Proof's '5 passed' = 3 existing + 2 new is correct; plan Files/Order/Risks/Options/Proof are internally consistent and the closed concern's decision matches spec.md. spec.md header equals `gate/cli.py spec-header` output byte for byte. intent.md is untouched (not in the diff).

Proof: ran the three targets at HEAD myself: `python -m compileall -q .` no output exit 0; `python -m pytest` '3 passed in 0.01s' exit 0; `python -m ruff check .` 'All checks passed!' exit 0 - identical to CLAUDE.md's healthy output and to gate-b.json's recorded runs. Ran `gate/cli.py check --dry-run` (local plugin 0.2.0): limits ok (iterations 2, cap 2), artifacts, design_scope, open_concerns, commands, guardrails, risk_list ('no risk-list item touched' - the round-1 hit is gone), owner_actions all ok; adversarial_review fails only as 'stale: verdict is for 87d0476' (expected; this file replaces it). The dry run wrote nothing; `git status` clean before and after.

Blast radius: `git diff --name-status origin/main...HEAD` touches only changes/0001-add-percent-helper-to-sample-pkg/** (spec.md, plan.md, status.yaml, evidence/*); no source, no guardrail file (.claude/**, CLAUDE.md, REVIEW.md, sdlc.yaml), no .env in the diff; working tree clean, no untracked files. .env was not read (it is tracked on main as the project's declared fixture; pre-existing, not part of this change). Branch is one commit behind origin/main (a33ab23, owner's bump of sdlc.yaml plugin pin 0.2.4->0.2.5); the branch does not touch sdlc.yaml so there is no conflict, and the spec header's '0.2.4' is the version in force when the spec was written on this branch (nit, not a defect).

Policies: coding-standards rules 2/4/7 cited and correct (no docstring matches calc.py; test_percent fails under the rejected operand order, so rule 4's 'test that fails without it' now holds for the formula too; small explicit function); security-baseline 'does not fully apply' verified against the skill text (pure arithmetic, no endpoint/input/secret/shell/SQL/file/dependency; rule 8 risk-list sentence reworded, gate agrees); data-conventions and ux-conventions 'does not apply' verified (no stored data, no UI, no displayed copy); spec-template rules held (concern closed by owner, questions answered, header pasted from the generator, intent.md not edited); definition-of-done (b) items present.

Tests: evaluated the pinned formula against the real divide for 18 inputs plus an exhaustive sweep (x/100 for x in 1..10000, and x/w for w in {1,2,4,5,8,10,20,25,50,100,200,1000}): every result equals Python's x*100/w and every x/100 returns exactly float(x); the rejected `divide(part, whole) * 100` returns 7.000000000000001 / 28.999999999999996 / 56.99999999999999 for 7, 29, 57 out of 100, so the planned `percent(7, 100) == 7.0` assertion now distinguishes the two and the tests cannot pass with the round-1 defect present. Zero whole (1/0, 0/0, 1/0.0) raises ZeroDivisionError('b must not be zero') via divide, matching spec Design. Pre-existing tests untouched; change_type feature, tests_locked false, so the fix-type test lock does not apply. Nit (not Important, magnitudes are unrealistic for a percent helper): scaling first overflows for |part| > ~1.8e306 - percent(1e307, 1e307) returns inf where the old order returned 100.0; both orders already return inf for 1e308/1.
